utterances.text: I think about 20 minutes after this conversation. They called me on the phone. I cannot remember now whether it was from the entrance desk or from the duty officers telling me that the commander was coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you describe your contact with Pandurevic when he arrived?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, I walked out of the office - this was my second exit during this relatively short meeting - with the intention of meeting him and reporting to him in front of the facility down there. However, I didn't have enough time to do so, because he came up as I had walked downstairs, and we meet downstairs, in front of the offices. We stopped briefly there and I informed him, briefly, about the prisoners and the operation of killing, execution, that Beara and Popovic took part in, and about the problems that Major Jokic had informed me about and familiarised me with at the moment when Vasic and I walked into the building of the brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And remember to be slow. I know it's getting late, but the translators are still working up there. What else did you say to Commander Pandurevic at this point? Or let me -- I'm sorry. Let me ask: After you reported to him that information, did he say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He asked me why the civilian defence was not doing the digging in. I didn't know. Nobody mentioned the civilian defence to me and I didn't know that they were supposed to be doing it. I simply shrugged. I did not have such information. Then he asked me about the column and about the 4th and 7th Battalions. I told him briefly that they were still at their respective positions, their defence positions. He asked me why the column had not been stopped earlier by using technical equipment. I told him that, quite simply, I could not have done it because they were too strong and the information coming in was confusing. And as we were saying that, we entered the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let me go back a bit. You said he responded to your report about the Muslim prisoners with a statement about why wasn't the civilian -- some civilian organisation digging in. What did he mean -- what do you think he meant by that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The civilian protection is an organisation which existed at that time. I think it still exists in our part of the world. It is supposed to give different kinds of assistance to the civilian population, and generally speaking, in an area when there are some emergencies, and so on. And he asked me why the civilian protection was not doing the digging.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What did you take "the digging" to relate to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Problems related to burying the executed prisoners. That's what it meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you and Mr. Pandurevic have any other discussion related to those prisoners, the executed prisoners -- burial, at the headquarters that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. It was the way I said it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So after you had a chance to inform him of the military situation, after talking to him about the prisoners; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. The first information I gave him was about the prisoners, and then, after that, a brief conversation, just a few sentences, about the military situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the meantime, we entered the office, my office, where the mentioned three officers from the MUP were already sitting. I was expecting Colonel Vasic to support me, since we had discussed this, that we were asking for permission for the column to be let through. And he opposed that. He said: No one had the right to trade in Serb land. And he asked me to familiarise him with the military situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When you said he opposed that, who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean our commander, Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When you had spoken to General Krstic prior to that, did you mention this idea of a corridor to General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. He practically interrupted me with the information that my commander was coming. And I realised that -- it was my understanding that the commander would resolve everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And so what happened after your commander opposed the idea of a corridor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I informed him. I briefed him, practically, about my knowledge as to the forces involved. I think I said that involved three groups of 2.000 men respectively, that this first group was the most dangerous one, from a combat point of view, for our units; and that they were just by the rear of our 4th and 7th Battalions. I think I said that they were in the region of Planinci and Krizevicke Njive and that the situation militarily speaking was not a rosy one at all. He then asked Colonel Vasic what he had available in terms of MUP forces, and Vasic said that Borovcanin was supposed to make all the decisions referring to the MUP. He appointed at Borovcanin and he said that he had a unit and he was waiting for another detachment to come from Janje and he was willing to make those units available for combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what else of significance that you can recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic said, classically, from a military point of view: I have decided to engage the Podrinje Detachment from Duga Kosa, from the positions of the 7th Battalion, and this police detachment of the civilian police from Janje from the direction of Parlog. There should be a counter-attack and the column of the 28th Division, or rather its forces, should be suppressed in the vicinity of Planinci, they should be surrounded there and asked to surrender. Also use all available artillery support in this. He appointed me to command the forces in Baljkovica. That is to say, the Podrinje Corps, the 4th Battalion, and this civilian police detachment that was supposed to come from Janje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. During the discussions in the commander's office that you've just spoken of, who else was present during this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was present. I already said when Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic came, together with me, at the very outset, was Colonel Vasic. We walked in together. A bit after Vasic and myself, perhaps, say, 15 minutes later - I cannot remember that exactly now - Borovcanin came, Lieutenant Colonel Borovcanin, and Stupar, together with him. These persons were certainly present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When Pandurevic arrived in the meeting, did it stay in your office or did it move over to his office, this meeting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. McCloskey. We stayed on in my office. We went straight in, through the door and into my office.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: During the discussions after Pandurevic arrived, were there any discussions of the operation to -- related to the Muslim prisoners in Zvornik or Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was there, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, prior to Vinko Pandurevic arriving, you have described the various discussions that you had with Borovcanin and Stupar, and Vasic. Aside from what you've already described, was there any discussions of the Muslim prisoners that were then in Zvornik still in detention on this, the afternoon of the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there weren't any such discussions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And after you received these orders from your commander to lead this group, did you go out and do that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Did you -- in the process of doing that, did you have any -- did you have any communication with anyone relating to the Muslim prisoners in the area of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you talk to anybody later on in the 4th Battalion area about Muslim -- about the Muslim prisoners?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, during the course of that afternoon, in fact. After we had stabilised the military situation, at least for a time, in the Baljkovica region, I talked to Lieutenant Lazar Ristic, perhaps for an hour or two at the most, after I arrived in Baljkovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what did you discuss with Lazar Ristic on this point?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I first asked him something with respect to the discussion we had on the afternoon of the 14th, I and his signalman. I asked him how come two days before that, when I asked him to make available a platoon for the ambush, he said he didn't have any available men, whereas he nonetheless had a group to send to Rakovac [as interpreted]. And he said that that particular afternoon, Captain Milorad Trbic phoned him up and at the time he was the referring officer in the Zvornik Brigade, and that he asked him urgently to send some soldiers, some men, because a problem had arisen in Orahovac, the school there. And what happened was that the prisoners wanted to break out. And Lazar Ristic sent seven or eight soldiers to help secure the prisoners in that school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. The record said that whereas he nonetheless had a group to send to Rakovac. Is that Rakovac? Is that correct? Or is it someplace else?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's a mistake, or perhaps I made a slip of the tongue. It was Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Was there any other discussion about that subject with Lazar Ristic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He told me that on that 14th, in the evening, he did go to see what was happening, because he was a little worried, as the school was in the middle of the village, in actual fact. And so when he arrived there, he found these seven or eight soldiers providing security for the prisoners in the school, guarding the prisoners in the school. And according to what he said, he lined them up to let them go, because -- to dismiss them because he saw what was going on, but Drago Nikolic, the second lieutenant, opposed this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What else did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me that Drago Nikolic had asked that the soldiers remain there guarding the prisoners, and if they do so, via Captain Milosevic, he would ensure new uniforms. He mentioned that he had seen a group of soldiers, and he didn't -- wasn't quite clear on where this group had come from. He considered that they were not soldiers from the Zvornik Brigade. They were in camouflage uniform, according to what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did he say anything else at that time about this subject?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The executions had already started when he stopped by at the school in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did he tell you anything else, what he did about it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If I remember correctly, that was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Had you received any information about whether or not any Zvornik Brigade soldiers took part in the executions near Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On two occasions. That same day, a little later on - whether it was in the corridor or in front of the building where the 4th Battalion had its headquarters - one of their rear servicemen came up to me and said he had heard that Lieutenant Colonel -- that second Lieutenant Nikolic had participated in the execution and that he was surprised. He just couldn't believe it how come this happened. At a later period, again I learnt -- rumours were going round by this time - that Koko Simic had taken part too - Gojko Simic, a man from the 4th Battalion. Later on, when I asked Lazar Ristic about that, he said that the man I mentioned was on leave. He was taking some free days because he was seeing his son off to the army. And otherwise he lived in Orahovac. And he joined the first group guarding the prisoners in the school building, and later on when Drago Nikolic asked for volunteers, he volunteered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What happened to Gojko Simic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gojko Simic was killed in the fighting on the 16th, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Later did you receive -- did you have any discussions with anyone from any of the other battalions about this operation to kill the Muslim prisoners, either that day or the following day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I talked about it that same day, but the next day, in the evening - that is to say, the 16th - towards evening, I met Captain first class Ostoja Stanisic, at Parlog, and I had a brief conversation with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who was he? What was his position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Captain first class Ostoja Stanisic was the commander of the 6th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And where was the commander -- where was the headquarters of the 6th Battalion located at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The headquarters of that particular battalion was situated in the village of Petkovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How close was that village to the large dam near Petkovci?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, approximately two kilometres away from the dam.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What did you learn from Mr. Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me that his deputy that day had been wounded and that he was left alone, and that the previous day, in the new school building in Petkovci, a group of prisoners had been executed directly in the school house and the outbuildings of the school, so that he had to engage part of his rear unit to take the corpses of the people killed away and to clean up the area. And he didn't like having to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What do you mean when you said his deputy had been wounded and that he was left alone? First of all, who is Ostoja Stanisic's deputy?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, the deputy of the commander of the 6th Battalion was Lieutenant Marko Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And do you recall Stanisic saying anything else to you about this subject?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he did mention that on the 14th, in the evening, the prisoners had been brought to the school in Orahovac, and all the rest as I have recounted it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did he mention any names of any VRS or others that were involved in that process?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He mentioned Colonel Beara.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what did he say about Beara?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he said that that group of prisoners had been brought there by Beara, this man Beara, and that they had organised the execution there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did he tell you what units actually committed the execution?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't tell me that at the time. I learnt later on that the people who participated were members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment from Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The fact that the 10th Sabotage Detachment murdered prisoners at Petkovci, did that change your responsibility at all regarding those killings?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't change it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, did you learn where the various burial sites were of the prisoners that were executed in Zvornik during this time period?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean up until the 16th?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I mean, well, any time between the 16th or thereafter.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Later on I learnt about the different sites where the executions had taken place and about the sites of the first burials.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you just briefly describe for us, and maybe with the pointer, just point out the general areas where the burials occurred.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, shall we start from this area here? I can see the dam and the lake at Petkovci. And within the frameworks of the dam, there was a site where the prisoners from the school in Petkovci were taken off and shot there, and they were buried there too in the vicinity. That's one place. I can't quite see from here where the school in Orahovac is, but generally in this area, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Where else?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And also around the school was where the burial sites were. The next place was the school in Rocevici, on the road from Zvornik as you go to Kozluk. And they were incarcerated there in the school by the road on the left-hand side, and those people were shot -- executed at Kozluk, on the banks of the Drina River, towards Zvornik, looking at it from Rocevici. The next place was Pilica, and two sites in Pilica, in actual fact. The cultural centre, Dom Kultura, whatever the building was called, right up by the road in the centre of Pilica, and the other place was further into the village, on this road here. The school house at a place called Kula, the prisoners from the school at Kula were taken off to the farm here in Pilica, towards the Lokanj Road, where they were executed and buried. The map is a little far away from me, and I can't quite show you the locations, but the name of the place is as I have stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What happened to the bodies after they were buried?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later on, in mid-September, I heard for the first time -- actually, it was on the 14th of September. I was in the field somewhere, and when I returned, the duty officer informed me that from the corps they had reported that Captain Trbic was to take over five tonnes of fuel. I found this a little suspicious. I was -- it seemed to be strange why Trbic should be asked to do that. So I called up the duty officer in the corps command and he said that he knew nothing about this but that he would check it out. A short while after that, Colonel Popovic called and asked me where I had got this information from about the fuel and Captain Trbic and I told him that the officers on duty, the operations duty officer from the corps headquarters had told me, and he made a joke - at least I took it to be a joke. He said they were incapable of seeing to the matter and that he would see to it himself as of that point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what else did you learn about Popovic's or anyone's activity relating to these reburials?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The following day, that is to say on the 15th, Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic came back from Krajina and I conveyed to him this information about the fuel and my conversation with the colonel, Colonel Popovic. He was going to the corps headquarters on that day, I mean Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic, was on the way to the HQ. And the following day we talked, and it was said that Popovic would transfer the bodies from those primary burial sites to others.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So who did --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To rebury them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just to make it clear: Who did you learn from that Popovic would be transferring the bodies from the primary sites?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my commander, Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that was when he returned from the Drina Corps headquarters?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When he went back, when he returned. I didn't go to the Drina Corps headquarters. He went. So when he returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. So when he returned is when he told you about what Popovic was going to do. Okay.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you learn anything else about this reburial process at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Sometime later - and actually, I remember the date. It was the 26th of September, and I remember the date because on that particular day I was supposed to go with a unit to Krajina, to Mrkonjic grad, in fact. So on the 26th, in the early morning hours, when I left, at the entrance, or rather, the stairs, the staircase in front of the HQ brigade building, I met Colonel Popovic. I shook hands with him and he asked me: Is your commander up there and is Drago up there? He meant Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic, of course, and second Lieutenant Drago Nikolic and I said both of them were up there. I left and he went into the building. I remember this vividly because he was carrying a topographic map with him, but it was rolled are up and not folded the way us army men do. It was a long roll of paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And where did you go after that, after that brief meeting with Popovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to Kozluk, where I was supposed to line up the unit that went to Krajina. And as the commander of that unit of the Drina Corps, I went together with the unit to Mrkonjic Grad, within the composition of the 1st Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you learn anything about the reburial process while you were on duty in the Krajina Corps area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't, Mr. McCloskey. There was fighting going on there against the units of the HVO and BH army. So we engaged in battle there. We were fighting. We had no particular connections to Zvornik at all, communication with Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And when did you return to Zvornik on duty?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, it was on the 20th of October, I believe, 1995, and afterwards I was given four or five days' leave, which I spent at home. So I might have been back with my unit sometime around the 25th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: After returning to Zvornik, did you learn any information about the reburials?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did learn about them. I learnt that during that period, this reburial took place, or rather, that the bodies were taken away from the sites the prisoners of Srebrenica had been executed and buried, that they had been transferred to other places, other sites.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you get any information about who actually did this reburial?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The reburials were being done under the control of Colonel Beara and Popovic, and from what I heard, the two of them in that area of Zvornik, and further afield where these activities were taking place, they would turn up wearing civilian clothing to oversee the whole process, and that Lieutenant Drago Nikolic took part in all that as well, and that Trbic, Captain Trbic handled the fuel and disposed of the fuel, which they filled the machine tanks with, the machinery they used to transport the bodies of the people executed. I also learnt during that time that the police, the military police of the Drina Corps, provided broader security around the area and blocked all traffic on the roads, on the communication lines, to enable the job to get done unimpeded. Several soldiers from our military police company, the military police company of the Zvornik Brigade, in fact, which Second Lieutenant Drago Nikolic took with him in order to provide traffic security or something along those lines, were also taken. And the other thing I learnt was that a couple of people from our engineers company had taken part working on those primary sites, primary burial sites, in loading up the corpses, and that Drago Nikolic and Popovic would replace the truck drivers on whose trucks the corpses were being loaded up so that nobody knew where the trucks were actually being taken. He would replace the drivers at regular intervals. And this was rumoured around pretty broadly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you learn the names of the people from the engineering company that were taking part in the digging up of the primary graves?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not, to be quite frank, I wasn't very interested in learning their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know whose machinery was involved in this digging and body transport process?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think several of our machines were used, one or two, one or two, actually, were used on the sites where the corpses were dug out of the primary burial sites. And as to the digging at the secondary sites, Popovic had brought in people from somewhere, whether from the engineering battalion of the Drina Corps or somewhere else, I really don't know. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Where did you get your information that two people from the Zvornik Brigade engineering company were involved in this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't mean two. I meant several. So I can't be quite precise on that score. But I heard that -- well, I can't really remember whether in talking to Drago Nikolic or perhaps Trbic or one of those people from our headquarters, from our command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Same question for the machinery of the engineering company of the Zvornik Brigade. Where did you learn that information from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was from Drago Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you ever speak to Dragan Jokic about that reburial operation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you have any information that he was involved in that reburial operation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really do not have any such knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Are you aware of any investigation made by anyone in the Zvornik Brigade into the abuses of the Muslims that came as prisoners to the Zvornik Brigade area in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any such information. I don't know of any investigation having been instituted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Are you aware of any Zvornik Brigade soldier that was punished for abusing Muslim prisoners in any way in that time period where prisoners came to the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, no, no one was punished, and I'm not aware of anyone having been punished.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Was there a system in place in the Zvornik area to punish soldiers that committed criminal offences while on duty or related to their military activities?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And were soldiers regularly investigated, tried, and punished for committing offences?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For some, yes, graver crimes like killings, woundings. Proceedings were started and carried out. Proceedings were also initiated for relatively minor crimes, and I don't know how efficient the process was, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I've got some exhibits. I probably won't get through them all tonight. I apologise about that. We can try to go through them or we can just maybe start fresher on Monday, whatever you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, -- yes, Ms. Sinatra.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, but Mr. McCloskey and I might meet between now and Monday and there may be some exhibits that we'll stipulate to, without having him go through the witness. If we come to an agreement that they're admissible and we have no objections to them, then we wouldn't have to present them through the witness. I'm offering to work with Mr. McCloskey on an agreement of stipulation on certain exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So you mean we'll stop here?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: No. It's totally up to you and up to Mr. McCloskey whether he has more evidence he needs to get through this witness, but I'm just talking about: There are some documents that we have no objections to and we could come to an agreement ahead of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We might save some time, Your Honour. We have been speaking frequently with counsel about logbooks and other things and we might be able to save some time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please inform us how much time do you need next Monday? Just give us a rough idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: One hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. So we'll resume next Monday at 9.00, and the hearing is adjourned.
